detail.abstract: Bespoke jewellery has been sold through a verbal, multi-handoff process for decades: a customer describes a vision, a sales consultant interprets it, a designer redraws it, a CAD engineer models it, and a workshop manufactures it. This paper introduces the Interpretation Cascade, a structural framework, grounded in classical and contemporary research on serial information transmission, explaining why sequential human interpretation chains lose fidelity in a way that training, documentation and quality-assurance processes can only ever partially correct. Three propositions are derived: fidelity loss compounds across handoffs (P1); conventional mitigation reduces loss at the margin but cannot resolve the structural dynamic (P2); and removing the chain, replacing it with one continuously shared, customer-confirmed digital specification, resolves the problem structurally rather than incrementally (P3). We evaluate this framework against evidence from an adjacent, well-quantified industry (construction rework economics), against the recent academic literature specifically applying generative AI to jewellery design, and against the broader collapse in generative AI and augmented-reality infrastructure cost that has made continuous multi-party 3D/AR collaboration commercially viable only in the last few years. We then present OrnaNext, a collaborative AI, AR and 3D platform built on this analysis, its three-module system architecture, its position relative to six identified competitors, and the combined technical background, jewellery CAD/CAM manufacturing and enterprise distributed-systems architecture, that positions its two co-founders to build it.

title: Institutional Configurations and Urban Divergence: A Long-Run Comparative Political Economy of Kolkata and Shenzhen, c. 1690–2024

detail.title: Institutional Configurations and Urban Divergence: A Long-Run Comparative Political Economy of Kolkata and Shenzhen, c. 1690–2024

declarations.declarationOfInterest: INDEPENDENT STUDY
declarations.ethicsApproval: NON APPLICABLE
declarations.funderStatement: SELF FUNDED

detail.abstract: Kolkata entered the twentieth century as the principal industrial and commercial city of eastern India and one of the largest metropolises in Asia, endowed with a deep-water port, an established jute and engineering complex, and a remarkable concentration of universities and scientific institutes. Shenzhen entered the late 1970s as a predominantly rural county on the Pearl River estuary, with a population of roughly three hundred thousand industrial base to speak of. Within six decades, the two cities had effectively exchanged positions in the global urban hierarchy. By 2024, Shenzhen's gross domestic product exceeded US$593 billion at constant 2015 prices, surpassing Hong Kong, while Kolkata's share of Indian manufacturing output had fallen below five per cent. The paper asks how, through which institutional mechanisms, and under what historical conditions such radically divergent trajectories emerged from initial endowments that pointed in the opposite direction. I develop a unified theoretical framework integrating new institutional economics, historical institutionalism, developmental-state theory, fiscal federalism, state-capacity theory, agglomeration economics, and path dependence into a single configurational model of urban growth. The framework identifies four binding mechanisms-land and factor markets, administrative incentive structures, labour regimes and migration, and the political settlement governing industrial policy-through which institutional arrangements amplify or suppress urban growth. Using a structured focused comparison, process tracing, within-case temporal analysis, and a quantitative reconstruction of city-level indicators from 1850 to 2024, we test the framework against ten rival hypotheses emphasising geography, initial endowments, global integration, human capital, technology, demography, institutions, state capacity, agglomeration, and configurational complementarity. The evidence indicates that no single rival explanation can account for the divergence. The strongest interpretation is an interacting institutional configuration that altered the returns to investment, the mobility of labour and capital, the provision of infrastructure, and the capacity of each city to generate and sustain agglomeration. These institutional effects were historically contingent, amplified through increasing returns, and mediated by national and global shocks. The paper contributes a methodological template for city-level comparative political economy, a refinement of the institutional-configurational thesis applied to urban rather than national outcomes, and a sceptical assessment of what two-case designs can and cannot establish about the causal role of institutions.

title: AI Search Features and Quality Degradation
affiliations: Michigan State University - Department of Economics

detail.title: AI Search Features and Quality Degradation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: Search platforms, such as Google and Bing, increasingly answer queries with artificial intelligence (AI) search features that scrape and synthesize content from online publishers. In this paper, I develop a theoretical model to examine how the introduction of AI search features affects content investment decisions, platform design choices, and welfare. Although improving AI content quality increases the direct benefit each user receives on the search platform, it also diverts users away from each publisher's site. This weakens the publishers' incentives to invest in high quality content indirectly reducing the quality of the AI content. Therefore, it is optimal for the search platform to degrade the quality of its AI search feature to temper this feedback effect. In face of this tradeoff, I show that AI search features improve user surplus, but may reduce social welfare if publishers sufficiently value user clicks. Applying my framework to several proposed policies, I find that copyright restrictions can implement the socially optimal outcome; platform competition reduces social welfare; and opt-out options, licensing deals, and pay-per-crawl payments have ambiguous effects on welfare.

title: Human-Based Versus Algorithmic-Based Treatments: Evidence from the Opioid Epidemic
affiliations: University of Washington, Tacoma, Harvard University - Harvard Kennedy School (HKS) and Georgetown University

detail.title: Human-Based Versus Algorithmic-Based Treatments: Evidence from the Opioid Epidemic

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No  competing interests to report.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding.

detail.abstract: The U.S. opioid epidemic motivated several federal prescribing guidelines, which nonetheless relied heavily on one-size-fits-all, human-based clinical judgment to navigate the complex tradeoff between the harms of opioid use and those of inadequately managed pain. We study whether algorithmic-based approaches can be developed to learn personalized, multi-modal, and costeffective pain treatment policies capable of improving on both observed clinical practice and CDC guidelines along this tradeoff. Using longitudinal claims data on over 2.7 million patients (2017-2022), we formulate multi-modal pain treatment as a sequential decision problem and apply two offline reinforcement learning algorithms to recommend opioid and non-opioid dose, dayssupply, and use of non-pharmacologic treatments. We evaluate the resulting policies against three benchmarks: observed clinical practice, and counterfactual implementations of the CDC's 2016 and 2022 prescribing guidelines. Both algorithmic policies outperform all three benchmarks on several dimensions, including cost-effectiveness. However, for a subset of patients, human-based clinical judgment is the superior option. Robustness checks on a separate Medicaid population and under class rebalancing preserve the main conclusions, with the cost-effectiveness gap widening under population shift. Comparing CDC guidelines, we find the more restrictive 2016 guideline outperforms its less restrictive 2022 revision, indicating that CDC's efforts in revising the guideline have not been fruitful. Overall, our findings indicate algorithmic-based approaches are more powerful in providing pain treatment recommendations. The analysis, however, identifies a non-trivial subset of patients for whom no algorithmic policy improves upon human-based clinical judgment, providing an explicit boundary for real-world deployment.

title: Capacity Constrained Battery Repurposing Optimization with Piece-wise Value Function
affiliations: University of Science and Technology of China, Anhui Polytechnic University, University of Science and Technology of China, University of Science and Technology of China and University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) - School of Management

detail.title: Capacity Constrained Battery Repurposing Optimization with Piece-wise Value Function

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None.
declarations.funderStatement: NSFC

detail.abstract: The accelerating retirement of electric-vehicle lithium-ion batteries creates an urgent environmental management challenge: heterogeneous retired cells must be repurposed into second-life packs to displace primary manufacturing, yet capturing this value requires two coupled decisions—how to group cells into fixed-size packs under a piece-wise tiered valuation rule, and when to scrap low quality inventory so it does not crowd out higher-value futurereassemblies.Weformulatethecapacity constrained battery repurposing problem as a finite-horizon Markov decision process and propose a two-stage framework that decouples high-frequency Regular Reassembly Planning (RRP) from low-frequency Periodic Scrap Screening (PSS). RRP is solved by a hybrid simulated-annealing metaheuristic (SA) that seeds a Metropolis main loop with multi-start capacity-constrained K-means and intensifies it via embedded Variable Neighborhood Descent; PSS is solved by a Monte Carlo rollout heuristic (MCR) that scores candidate thresholds through rolling-horizon simulation with progressive candidate elimination. Computational experiments show that SA delivers both higher reward and lower runtime than VNS and GA on single-period instances and inside the full two stage system. Under a stress test with binding capacity and non-stationary arrivals, MCR achieves the highest average reward among all evaluated outer policies—exceeding every static-threshold rule, including the industry-default retain-all baseline—with the advantage growing monotonically with inner-solver strength. Sensitivity analysis over pack size, tier prices, and salvage value yields layered managerial guidance: operators should treat periodic scrapping as a quality-preservation lever and, where pack architecture is configurable at the product-design stage, minimise pack size subject to the heterogeneity budget, while regulators should concentrate fiscal instruments on the mid tier and complement aggregate waste-volume metrics with operational indicators.

detail.abstract: Because the traditional static Value-at-Risk (VaR) model assumes normality, it is unable to reflect the magnitude of severe losses during periods of systemic market stress effectively. To address the above problems, this paper builds a forward-looking and dynamic risk measurement system for the Hong Kong stock market based on a covariate-dependent Peaks-over-Threshold Generalized Pareto Distribution (POT-GPD). Daily log returns of the Hang Seng Index (HSI) and lagged CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) observations from January 2010 to July 2026 are used in the analysis to separate conditional tail risk into exceedance frequency and conditional severity. According to the results of logistic regression, a general market panic index, such as the VIX, is positively associated with the likelihood of an extreme tail event. At the same time, Maximum Likelihood Estimation also shows that modelling the GPD scale parameter as a log-linear function of the VIX successfully captures the amplification of expected excess losses during global volatility spillovers. The resulting time-varying VaR and Expected Shortfall (ES) indicators respond rapidly to changes in market volatility. Although the Kupiec Proportion of Failures test does not reject the null hypothesis of correct unconditional coverage of the 99% dynamic VaR, marginal residual tail clustering indicates remaining temporal dependence in tail events. Finally, the parsimonious EVT framework offers a high-responsiveness tool for capital optimisation and reduction of exposure to liquidity shocks in deeply interconnected global markets for quantitative risk managers and clearinghouses.

detail.abstract: Heuristically, the paper seeks to understand the religious perception of Africans otherwise regarded as the indigenous people and their contact with the missionary message. It adopts a historical, hermeneutical, and critical interpretation of some preconceived ideas about Africans as well as their reactions to the gospel message. It discovers that the introduction of the faith was done with clear intentions; slavery and economic exploitation, prejudices, and hence the demeaning attitude and bastardisation of the rich socio-cultural background of the people. However, the wisdom of the continent paved the way for the accommodation of messages. The paper concludes by recommending the following as some of the way forward: the messenger bearing the message should seek to know the socio-cultural background of African tradition, the Jesus' attitude of non-condemnation should be adopted as a global standard for all missionary volunteers to present-day Africa in order to put on record the right perspective about the people and lastly, African charismatic which has played a dominant role in the daily lives of the people has been enculturated into the life of the churches in Africa as evidenced in the dance pattern and gospel music, these should be greatly encouraged.

detail.abstract: This article examines how Michael Crichton's novels can help us understand how organizations and societies make sense of innovation and technological complexity, uncertainty, and conflicting values when confronting grand challenges. It presents technofear and technosolutionism as contrasting but interconnected ways of interpreting technological situations and justifying action. Based on a narrative analysis of The Andromeda Strain, The Terminal Man, Prey, and State of Fear, the study shows that these responses can coexist, alternate, and generate one another. Attempts to restore control can create new dependencies, reduce transparency, and blur responsibility, thereby generating technofear. Conversely, fear rarely leads to the abandonment of technology. Instead, it often encourages reliance on alternative experts and specific forms of knowledge. The article develops a dynamic framework for understanding this recursive relationship and presents fiction as a resource for innovation management, managerial reflection, foresight, and responsible innovation. Fiction is not treated as evidence of managerial behaviour or as validation of scientific claims. Rather, it provides material for examining how narratives construct and challenge claims about technological certainty, responsibility, control, and legitimacy.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces Human–AI Decision Integration Coaching (HAIDIC), a hybrid framework that positions algorithmic tools as information-processing instruments within — never replacements for — the accountability chain of executive coaching. Building on agency theory as a strategic heuristic (Eisenhardt, 1989; Jensen & Meckling, 1976) and on the concept of hybrid intelligence (Dellermann et al., 2019), the framework assigns moral and legal responsibility exclusively to human agents while exploiting the algorithm's comparative advantage in evidence aggregation and bias detection. The paper operationalizes decision quality (DQ) as a latent construct estimated through structural equation modeling, states three falsifiable propositions, and specifies the boundary conditions under which each party of the human–AI dyad holds a genuine performance advantage. The contribution is methodological as much as theoretical: it converts a rhetorically appealing idea into a testable research program.

detail.abstract:
The Financial Services AI Risk Management Framework (FS AI RMF) gives community banks 230 control objectives but not a common language for deciding what their artifacts establish. Banks may also depend on vendor systems they are responsible for governing but cannot unilaterally change. This position paper offers a translation ontology for coordination among banks, examiners and regulators, and vendors and architects, with affected parties as its normative center. Empty-chair representation asks whose interest a control protects when that party is absent from an AI-supported decision. 

      The ontology follows an affected interest through control objective, evidentiary object, available artifact, claimed inference and binding, and the actor able to close, disclose, or contest a gap. Decision records, feature attributions, local approximations, generated rationales, human review records, and approvals expose different objects; none inherits another's warrant merely by being called an explanation. The evidentiary-substitution sequence names that structure neutrally; silence-manufacture names instances in which unavailable contradictory evidence helps an unsupported substitution persist. 

      Three two-layer diagnostics first orient inquiry and then structure any authorized evidence request: empty-chair enumeration, pages missing from the ledger relative to a declared attestation scope, and the produced-silence question pair. They motivate five provisional evidentiary capabilities: revision-aware temporal capture; evidence binding and exportability; non-collapsing uncertainty representation; technical-change monitoring; and institutional-conformance monitoring. Worked applications to selected FS AI RMF controls illustrate the vocabulary rather than validate it across the framework. The paper supplies neither an implementation validation nor new examination authority; it identifies where current claims, technical capabilities, institutional obligations, and policy choices should meet.

title:
Cooling the Global South in an Increasingly Hotter World: 
Affordable Cooling and Climate Resilience for Sustainable Economic Development

detail.title:
Cooling the Global South in an Increasingly Hotter World: 
Affordable Cooling and Climate Resilience for Sustainable Economic Development

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal or financial relationships that could be perceived to have influenced the research. The study was conducted independently by H Heuristics Research & Advisory.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The study did not involve human or patient participants. All data used were secondary, aggregated, and publicly available from international sources (IEA, UNEP, IFC, FAO, World Bank). Therefore, formal ethics approval was not required.

detail.abstract:
Cooling has shifted from a discretionary household amenity to a core pillar of development infrastructure. As global temperatures rise and urban heat islands intensify, 3.5 billion people now live in climates where cooling determines health, productivity, and food security, yet only ~15% own an air conditioner. This access gap mirrors income gradients both across and within countries, producing sharply unequal protection from extreme heat. As the report notes, “Heat-related deaths among people over 65 rose 61% between 2002–04 and 2019–21,” while “air conditioning is estimated to have averted roughly 190,000 deaths annually by the end of that period.”

The economic consequences are equally severe. Extreme heat already erodes the equivalent of 31 million full‑time jobs annually, with South Asia facing a projected 7% GDP loss by 2050. Informal workers—who dominate labor markets across the Global South—can lose ~40% of earnings during a single heatwave, while inadequate cold-chain infrastructure destroys 526 million tonnes of food each year, costing 470 million smallholder farmers ~15% of their income.

Despite an estimated $8 trillion cumulative opportunity in sustainable cooling markets by 2050, financing remains the binding constraint. Cooling-specific investment needs total $400–800 billion, yet global adaptation finance reached only $26 billion in 2023, far below the $310–365 billion annual need projected by 2035.

To identify where cooling deficits convert most rapidly into mortality and economic loss, the report applies the Compound Vulnerability Multiplier—the product of D‑Coefficient (absorptive capacity), P‑Integral (cumulative heat burden), and Exposure Density (concentration of vulnerable populations). This framework underpins the proposed FLOW Framework:

  • Finance — blended and concessional capital, Cooling‑as‑a‑Service, and results‑based finance to de-risk adoption.

  • Leapfrog — passive design and efficient, Kigali‑compliant equipment to avoid locking in inefficient cooling stock.

  • Optimize — district cooling, standards, and refrigerant transition to bend demand and emissions curves.

  • Widen — targeted expansion into informal settlements and smallholder cold chains where vulnerability is highest.

Together, these pillars outline a pathway for the Global South to build cooling systems that are affordable, efficient, and climate‑resilient, avoiding the carbon‑intensive trajectory industrialized economies followed and closing the cooling access gap before rising heat makes it unmanageable.

detail.abstract: A frictionless view holds that intermediaries do not affect asset prices because households alone determine valuations. A simple model of delegation shows instead that prices reflect a weighted average of households' and intermediaries' subjective beliefs, with household influence determined by delegation strength, risk attitudes, and intermediaries' regulatory and contractual incentives. We use investor surveys to recover household influence as a time-varying latent process. We reject the frictionless view even in the stock market, arguably the least intermediated major asset class, while showing that the growth of intermediation substantially overstates the dilution of household influence. We link fluctuations in influence to risk, financial constraints, and the regulatory and technological forces reshaping US markets.

detail.title: Antitrust Remedies for Tech Monopoly

detail.abstract:
The antitrust courts have been increasingly reluctant to award structural remedies – i.e., “breakups” – in cases finding unlawful monopolization.  This is in contrast to consummated mergers, where spinning off of unlawfully acquired assets is the preferred remedy.  One problem with structural relief in monopolization cases is that identifying “fault lines” where a breakup could occur is very difficult for internally developed assets, and the courts have not been good at that.  Another problem is achieving a breakup that actually “improves competitive conditions,” as the Supreme Court has required.  A remedy that does not succeed in bringing prices down, output up, or in removing restraints on quality or innovation, is a failure.

All of these limitations are doubly true in big tech markets, particularly when the relevant assets are digital.  Most functional digital assets cannot be broken up without ruining them.  Once they are broken apart they simply become nonfunctional or at least noncompetitive.  On the other hand, one attribute of digital assets is that they can be licensed.  Nonexclusive licenses can actually be superior to breakups, creating what amounts to perfect competitors in the licensed technology.

title: The Constitutional Trap in Post-catch-up Economies: Time Horizons, Dual Externalities, and Coordination Capacity

detail.title: The Constitutional Trap in Post-catch-up Economies: Time Horizons, Dual Externalities, and Coordination Capacity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by the Ministry of Education of the Republic of Korea and the National Research Foundation of Korea (NRF-2023S1A5B5A17088175).

detail.abstract:
This paper explains why post-catch-up economies simultaneously experience innovation slowdown, demographic collapse, regional hollowing, youth incorporation failure, and persistent limitations in currency internationalization. Rather than treating these as separate failures, the paper interprets them as manifestations of a common upstream coordination constraint: when electoral-cycle pressures and capital liberalization interact with centralized policy structures organized around compressed constitutional time horizons, policy durability weakens and conditions for long-horizon coordination erode. The central mechanism operates through the absence of intermediate coordination layers relationship-based finance, vocational ecosystems, and decentralized coordination structures — which translate institutional durability into economic performance. These
layers emerge endogenously when policy continuity becomes credibly observable, most
notably through constitutional central bank independence. At the micro level, dual
externalities sustain this trap: actors supplying reform cannot internalize long-term
benefits accruing to future generations and peripheral regions, while actors choosing
inaction bear none of the costs imposed on others — systematically generating
under-supply of reform and over-supply of inaction.
The paper analyzes this mechanism through a structured comparison of Mexico and
Korea, which share similar hard-scope conditions but diverged in constitutional
commitment. Mexico's entrenchment of central bank independence produced partial
horizon alignment — enabling nominal stability and currency deliverability — without
generating full coordination capacity; Korea failed to achieve even this, producing
stronger coordination-failure pressures across domains. These findings imply that
restoring long-horizon coordination requires sequential constitutional reform: temporal
entrenchment must precede the emergence of decentralized coordination structures.
More broadly, sustainable prosperity under frontier conditions depends not on allocative
efficiency alone, but on constitutional architecture anchored in human dignity that
makes long-horizon coordination and cross-generational capability formation collectively
self-sustaining.

title: What Economic Integration is Viable in Africa?

detail.title: What Economic Integration is Viable in Africa?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: African integration is usually described as having failed. Over the same period in which the Abuja Treaty's six-stage sequence stalled at the regional customs-union and monetary-union stages, however, a parallel set of projects outside that sequence-the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System, one-stop border posts, and the AfCFTA Guided Trade Initiative-emerged and advanced. This paper argues that integration outcomes in Africa are sorted by two properties of the projects themselves: whether a project complements or substitutes for existing sovereign arrangements, and whether the benefits it promises are credible to the states deciding whether to commit. Projects that complement existing arrangements and offer credible benefits advance, because rational states have every reason to commit; projects that substitute for them and offer non-credible benefits stall, because no rational state should commit. The implementation gap in African integration is therefore not at the state level but at the project level. The framework is evaluated through two paired comparisons and used to derive policy implications, including the production-alliance-firm as a route for making deeper integration defensible over time.

detail.abstract: In various legal systems, trade secrets owned by business owners are protected. Such protection, however, has limits, and one of them is the scenario in which employees who have gained access to their employer's trade secret leave that company to practice their profession or trade elsewhere, which involves the use of knowledge or skills related to that trade secret. The purpose of this text is to examine this exception to trade secret protection in the context of comparative law and to propose an interpretation of it under Chilean law. Resolving this issue is not merely theoretical but particularly practical, since the majority of cases involving the misappropriation of trade secrets involve employees who leave their positions to take on new roles elsewhere, and if they are sued, the main defense they raise is that the allegedly misappropriated information has become part of their personal skills or knowledge, and therefore they are free to use it. In the specific case of Chilean law, this paper proposes resolving this dilemma by presenting a two-step test that first determines whether the trade secret has become inseparably integrated into the employee's person and, subsequently, determines whether the protection of the trade secret in question would affect the mobility of the employee involved in the litigation.

detail.abstract: Exchange rates obey a factor structure.  But do factor exposures enlighten economists beyond risk and return?  We argue currency risk amplifies transient spikes in foreign uncertainty that restrict foreign inward investment.  We call this effect carry-amplification, develop a novel theory of it, and test it empirically.  We find supporting evidence in country-level aggregates and in firm-level supply chain micro data. The effects concentrate in emerging markets and we contend that, over a long period of time, greater currency factor exposure can dampen their economic growth.

detail.abstract: This paper asks whether artificial intelligence is changing the prevalence of growthoriented entrepreneurship. In a commuting-zone-by-sector panel of U.S. workers, we compare sectors with differing AI exposure within the same commuting zone and year, absorbing every shock common to a place. A one-standard-deviation increase in AI exposure lowers the incorporated self-employment share by 0.401 percentage points (10.8% of baseline) in 2019-2024, while unincorporated self-employment shows no response. The decline first emerges in 2019, four years after the deep-learning era began, and is concentrated in the managerial and professional occupations from which incorporated business owners are drawn.

detail.abstract:
This book offers a comprehensive political-economic analysis of China's historical development and its contemporary rise, tracing continuities between imperial governance structures and the institutional foundations of the modern Chinese state. The central thesis holds that China's distinctive trajectory—from ancient collectivist civilization to industrial and technological power—reflects a coherent institutional logic rather than a series of disconnected historical episodes.

The analysis begins by locating the roots of Chinese "collectivism" in the recurring ecological challenges of flood control along the Yellow and Yangtze Rivers and in persistent nomadic threats, which together drove the evolution from the Western Zhōu enfeoffment system toward centralized bureaucratic rule under the Qín and Hàn dynasties. The adoption of Confucianism as state ideology and the subsequent development of the imperial examination system created what the book terms a "Confucian open society," in which governance was shared between emperors and examination-selected elites. This meritocratic mechanism, the book argues, prevented the entrenchment of hereditary aristocratic power and the concentration of land-based wealth, thereby sustaining centuries of political unification even as private land tenure expanded.

Turning to the modern era, the book frames the Communist Party of China's institutional capacity—rather than any single policy—as the decisive factor in national development. It traces a lineage from Soviet-style Five-Year Planning in the early PRC period, through the introduction of market mechanisms after 1978, to a distinctive hybrid model combining state direction with market forces. This "China Model" is credited with building manufacturing capacity, infrastructure, and, since 2012, a financial regulatory framework explicitly oriented toward long-term socialist development goals and technological self-sufficiency.

A substantial portion of the book addresses China's trajectory relative to the United States, forecasting continued geopolitical and technological rivalry through roughly 2040, based on a claimed historical pattern of thirty-year cycles in international relations. It links this forecast to the expansion of Chinese high-tech enterprises and the Belt and Road Initiative as vehicles for South-South economic cooperation, projecting eventual Chinese breakthroughs in strategically contested technologies.

The book further contends that China's post-1978 economic transformation should be understood not as a rejection of its earlier planned economy but as a continuation that unlocked latent capacities—administrative experience, industrial infrastructure, and a trained workforce—accumulated during the pre-reform decades. This argument extends into an examination of how China's "socialist market economy" emerged through incremental Party-led decisions rather than a predetermined blueprint, producing a diverse economic ecosystem of state, private, and foreign enterprises. The author positions this experience as a challenge to conventional Western developmental economics, which typically presumes that formal institutions must precede growth rather than co-evolve with it.

The concluding chapter situates China's rise within broader global patterns of industrialization, poverty reduction, and great-power competition, citing contemporary events—including the 2021 withdrawal from Afghanistan and 2026 US-Iran tensions—as evidence of the limits of military power against unified nations. It closes by casting China as a stabilizing force for developing nations navigating industrialization amid ongoing risks of great-power conflict and nuclear instability.

Overall, the book presents an integrated historical-institutional narrative connecting imperial statecraft, Communist Party governance, and China's contemporary global positioning, written from a perspective sympathetic to the achievements of the Chinese political-economic model.

detail.abstract: Doda district, situated in the Chenab Valley of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir, is characterized by rugged mountain topography, dispersed settlements, and marked geographical isolation, conditions that are widely understood to compound social and economic disadvantage in Himalayan regions. This study examines the spatial pattern of socioeconomic inequality across the seventeen tehsils of Doda district using secondary data drawn from the Census of India (2011) and the District Census Handbook of Doda. Twelve demographic and socioeconomic indicators encompassing total, General, Scheduled Caste (SC), and Scheduled Tribe (ST) population; sex ratio; literacy rate; main-worker employment rate; and the inter-group (General versus SC+ST) gaps in literacy, sex ratio, and employment were compiled tehsil-wise, mapped, and combined into a composite index of social inequality through a standardised ranking procedure. The results show a pronounced core-periphery pattern: Bhaderwah, Gundna, Assar, and Bhalla emerge as the least unequal, better-performing tehsils (composite scores between 1.33 and 5.25), while Bharath Bagla, Bhalessa (Gandoh), Kahara, Bhella, Mohalla, and, most acutely, Phigsoo (composite score 14.42) constitute a cluster of highly disadvantaged, peripheral tehsils. Literacy and employment gaps between the General and SC+ST populations are widest in and around Bhaderwah and Doda tehsils, while sexratio disparities peak in Thathri. The findings indicate that remoteness, terrain, and distance from the district headquarters interact with caste-based and gender-based disadvantage to reproduce durable, tehsil-level inequality. The paper concludes with a set of spatially targeted policy recommendations aimed at economic empowerment, educational access, healthcare delivery, gender equity, and inclusive infrastructure planning in the most disadvantaged tehsils.

detail.abstract: We examine how the 2018-2019 US-China trade war affected Mexican local labor markets. Combining monthly administrative records with regional differences in exposure to US tariffs on Chinese goods, we find that the war increased formal industrial employment and remuneration. The positive wage effects spilled over into the services sector. The gains are concentrated in regions treated early, whose initial employment structure was substantially more manufacturing-intensive than that of later-treated regions. Cohort composition, rather than delayed adjustment, explains the pooled dynamics. The results suggest that the positive labor effects from the trade war depended on existing industrial capacity and generated benefits beyond directly exposed production, extending into the broader local economy.

detail.abstract: Water is the only economic good that nothing can replace-and at the same time one of the most underpriced. Four billion people experience severe water scarcity for at least one month a year, two-thirds of the world's river basins now carry too much or too little water, and with the data centres of artificial intelligence a new large consumer has arrived. title: Credit Cycle Versus Commodity Cycle: A Regime-conditional Framework for Sector-Rotation Timing Between Large-cap Banks and High-dividend Coal Miners on the Indonesia Stock Exchange

detail.title: Credit Cycle Versus Commodity Cycle: A Regime-conditional Framework for Sector-Rotation Timing Between Large-cap Banks and High-dividend Coal Miners on the Indonesia Stock Exchange

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I don't have any personal or financial relationship with other people or organizations that may have or could be perceived to have influenced my study.

detail.abstract: Indonesia's benchmark equity index is dominated by two large-capitalization clusters that respond to structurally different macroeconomic drivers: systemically important banks (BBCA, BMRI, BBNI, BBRI), whose valuations are primarily a function of the domestic credit cycle and Bank Indonesia's policy rate, and high-payout thermal coal exporters (ITMG, BSSR), whose earnings and dividends track the US-dollar-denominated Newcastle coal benchmark, a price series subject to boom-bust supercycle dynamics driven by Chinese and Indian demand, weather, and geopolitics. Because these two return-generating mechanisms are largely independent of one another over multi-year horizons, and because each has historically produced identifiable, if noisy, turning-point signals — a peaking-and-pausing policy rate for banks, and a price approaching the marginal cost of production for coal — this paper argues that a regime-conditional rotation strategy between the two clusters is more defensible, on both diversification and timing grounds, than a static buy-and-hold allocation to either. Drawing on the bank interest-rate-sensitivity literature (Flannery & James, 1984; English, Van den Heuvel, & Zakrajšek, 2018), the commodity supercycle literature (Jacks, 2019; Erten & Ocampo, 2013), the dividend-signaling literature (Fama & French, 1988; Michaely, Thaler, & Womack, 1995), and the sector-rotation literature (Conover, Jensen, Johnson, & Mercer, 2008), this paper develops a two-axis regime matrix — policy-rate direction against commodity-price-forecast direction — together with a four-stage barbell rotation checklist for moving capital between the two clusters. A fifteen-year historical mapping of the Indonesian market (2011–2026) illustrates the framework's internal consistency, and the framework is applied to conditions prevailing in August 2026, in which Bank Indonesia's policy rate had just entered a pause after a cumulative 100-basis-point tightening cycle while Newcastle coal remained priced above its own three-year-forward consensus, as an exploratory case illustration. An agenda for controlled backtesting against a monetary-conditions rotation benchmark and a time-series-momentum benchmark is proposed.

detail.abstract: Multivariate analysis of variance and covariance test whether groups differ on correlated responses, but the classical statistics and the multivariate Welch analogue (Johansen 1980) assume a common covariance and run liberal under the unequal covariances, small samples, and skew common in practice: at a four-group, two-dimensional corner (variance ratio 8, six per group) the plug-in Wald test reaches size 0.37 and Johansen 0.13, while the known-covariance oracle stays near nominal. We carry the guaranteed-level construction from one-way ANOVA (T_BB, a Berger-Boos deflation of the Welch quadratic) to the multivariate mean-vector problem and covariate adjustment. The guaranteed test deflates the Johansen reference by a factor exp(κ √ A) built from the design instability; a fixed constant holds size across a 160-design grid, and a design-adaptive constant recovers about half its power cost while tracking the oracle. The guarantee is empirical within a stated envelope, validated out-of-sample on an expanded grid (non-proportional and near-singular covariances, variance ratios to 32, adverse imbalance): a re-pinned constant controls all 172 held-out designs. At matched size the radius and Johansen are the same statistic, so the radius trades conservativeness, not efficiency, for the guarantee. The scalar closed form does not transfer: the radius is closed form in a pxp trace and no smaller, though two analytic radii, one proved over the entire Gaussian nuisance, bound the level. Under covariate adjustment the corner persists; heterogeneity of regression, a new bias axis, is handled by a slope-homogeneity screen, and a minimum-sample-size design guide states the per-group n the test needs.

detail.abstract: This study investigates the impact of ambiguity and other uncertainty shocks on business cycles using an event constraint SVAR approach. We find that ambiguity contributes to output fluctuations, and positive ambiguity shocks raise production. Both financial uncertainty and ambiguity are exogenous shocks to production, but they have opposite effects. Moreover, this study explores the relationships between these shocks, showing that positive ambiguity shocks increase other uncertainty measures. Furthermore, it is revealed that financial uncertainty shocks decrease ambiguity, whereas policy uncertainty shocks do not have an impact on ambiguity.

title: Schema-Boundedness Why Redundant Verification Fails Precisely on the Events that Matter

detail.title: Schema-Boundedness Why Redundant Verification Fails Precisely on the Events that Matter

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.funderStatement: none

detail.abstract:
Institutional designs for improving information quality under hierarchy model a report as a number, x it = θ t + ϵ it + b it. This presupposes that an observation has already been recognised as an instance of θ. Real channels are not general-purpose observers; they are classifiers with fixed codomains. Before a number is transmitted, some agent must decide which quantity this is an observation of, and only observations mapping into a pre-existing category can be reported at all. 

I call this schema-boundedness and derive four analytical results. (i) The return to channel redundancy is positive on the visible region and zero on the region no schema covers, so measured accuracy can improve without limit while total epistemic capacity is flat. (ii) Dispersion diagnostics computed on emitted reports cannot separate "no event" from "an event outside every schema." (iii) Scoring reporters on value accuracy relocates bias from the scored dimension (the value) to the unscored one (the category), a multitask distortion in the sense of Holmström and Milgrom (1991); under stated sufficient conditions the centre's loss is U-shaped in the accuracy weight λ, so accuracy scoring has an interior optimum and must be tuned, not maximised; the optimum is itself non-monotone in the severity of classification scoring, so weak classification scoring lowers the optimal accuracy weight before strong scoring raises it. (iv) Because schemas are patched after realised events, the blind set concentrates in the high-surprisal region-a consequence I derive from the patching rule rather than assume. 

Monte Carlo simulations verify the implementation, check the sufficient conditions at explicit calibrations, and characterise finite-sample behaviour; they do not prove the propositions, and the two are kept separate throughout. Under fully shared schemas, measured RMSE falls by a factor of 5.7 from n=1 to n=32 channels while true RMSE falls 34%, the ratio of apparent to real improvement rising to 1.99. The interior optimum sits at λ * = 1.624 in the baseline calibration and all four sufficient conditions hold there; maximising λ instead raises loss by 44.1%. 

The paper's empirical content is a frozen pre-registration, not a finding, and this version reports five corrections to v1.0 found by running the checks a referee would have run. The most consequential is that heterogeneous threshold definitions reduce the detectability of manipulation by a factor of eleven while leaving its magnitude statistically unchanged-so the diagnostic itself is subject to capture, and any real test must pair the density statistic with an external criterion.

title: The Carry-unwind Shortcut: JGB Curve Location, Volatility States, and Global FX Repricing

detail.title: The Carry-unwind Shortcut: JGB Curve Location, Volatility States, and Global FX Repricing

detail.abstract: Market commentary often compresses a rise in Japanese government bond yields into a single causal chain: yen funding becomes more expensive, carry trades unwind, and global risk assets reprice. This paper tests the empirical content of that label. Using daily Japanese yield-curve innovations, a 12-currency exposure panel, and a separately constructed non-yen high-minus-low carry factor from 2013 through July 2026, the design separates short-end from long-duration shocks, positive from negative repricing, and high-from normal-volatility states. The carry-unwind signature is sharply conditional. In the currency panel, positive short-end shocks produce a stronger five-day loss gradient among economies with larger predetermined yen-credit exposure only in high-volatility states; the interaction survives Holm correction (p = 0.018), and the positive-minus-negative high-volatility contrast also survives (p = 0.010). In the separately constructed carry factor, the total slope on positive short-end repricing is negative at one and five days in high-volatility states, with Holm-adjusted p-values of 0.016 and 0.018. Negative short-end and long-duration shocks are close to zero. Event paths are directionally consistent but weaker: funding-type shocks are followed by a 1.51% twenty-day carry loss versus 0.31% after duration-type shocks, with a suggestive difference (p = 0.064). A 90th-percentile volatility threshold and release-lag checks preserve the main ordering. The evidence supports a state-contingent classification, not a generic causal claim: carry unwind is not a synonym for rising JGB yields.

title: Cycle phenotypes and a graph attention transformer for outcome prediction in in vitro fertilization

detail.title: Cycle phenotypes and a graph attention transformer for outcome prediction in in vitro fertilization
detail.abstract: Background and Objectives: Assessment of an in vitro fertilization (IVF) cycle spans patient characteristics, ovarian response, laboratory performance and transfer outcome, yet no single indicator captures their interaction or differences in case mix. We asked whether routine IVF data contain reproducible cycle phenotypes, and whether a graph attention transformer trained on a patient-similarity network adds prognostic information to a tabular neural ensemble.,Methods: Five datasets from five centers were analyzed: 1,556 fresh stimulated cycles for phenotype development, 172 for external assessment, 1,172 for graph model development, 75 consecutive prospective cycles for graph audit and 791 frozen embryo-transfer cycles for case-mix analysis. Eighteen standardized variables entered k-means clustering, evaluated by silhouette, Calinski–Harabasz and Davies–Bouldin indices. An untrained weighted-cosine similarity graph audited phenotype coherence (Mann–Whitney U test). A graph attention transformer was trained under transductive five-fold cross-validation and compared with the tabular ensemble.,Results: Clustering identified lower-yield (n = 432), standard-yield (n = 807) and higher-yield (n = 317) phenotypes; 17 of 18 variables differed. Three-cluster silhouette coefficients were 0.186 in development and 0.190 externally. Within-phenotype graph edges were more similar than between-phenotype edges (median 0.897 versus 0.807; P < 0.001). Out-of-fold, the graph model reached an AUC of 0.632, a Brier score of 0.241 and an F1 score of 0.623 at the cross-validation-derived threshold of 0.49, against 0.652 and 0.233 for the tabular ensemble. The two models correlated moderately (r = 0.79), and their weighted combination reached an AUC of 0.658–0.665 and a Brier score of 0.229.,Conclusions: Routine IVF data contain reproducible cycle-yield phenotypes with convergent graph-structural support. Patient-similarity learning carries a partially independent signal that improves calibration in combination with tabular modeling, but does not surpass it alone.

detail.abstract: The development of synthetic biology is characterised by two approaches to innovation, based on intellectual property rights and sharing initiatives. This article examines this tension, arguing that some parts of the synthetic biology scientific community are adopting sharing initiatives due to perceived innovation impediments caused by the patent system. Using an empirical approach, the article analyses the OpenPlant case study through the knowledge commons framework. The study identifies significant potential impediments associated with patenting in synthetic biology, as well as relevant benefits and implications that arise from the adoption of a commons model. The analysis sheds light on what drives synthetic biologists to embrace a "knowledge commons" or sharing approach and how this practice can positively impact innovation.

title: Future Mobility: Electric, Autonomous, Connected, Shared -How Investors can Take Part in the Remaking of Transport

detail.title: Future Mobility: Electric, Autonomous, Connected, Shared -How Investors can Take Part in the Remaking of Transport

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No one influenced this study
declarations.funderStatement: No funder

detail.abstract:
Transport is undergoing its greatest transformation since the horse carriage gave way to the motor car: in 2025 one in four new cars sold worldwide was electric, driverless taxis complete roughly half a million paid rides a week in American metropolitan areas, and software is turning the vehicle from a product of mechanical craftsmanship into a computer on wheels. This paper-the first of six devoted to the great megatrends-orders the field of future mobility along its five arenas: decarbonisation and alternative drive systems, autonomous driving, connectivity, shared mobility, and the urban transformation including micromobility.

The paper examines market positions and timetables: battery prices have fallen by
more than 90 per cent since 2010 (2025: USD 108 per kilowatt-hour), five-minute
charging is series production reality in China, driverless lorries have been running
in Texas since 2025, and the robotaxi market could grow to more than USD 400
billion by 2035 — while the privately owned Level 4 car is, by broad agreement,
unlikely before the 2030s and will dominate the vehicle fleet only decades later. For
investors, the paper names listed companies along the entire value chain — large
and mid caps exclusively — with their business ideas and trading venues, and
identifies two ETFs that pass the selection checklist developed in the text.

The investment conclusion cuts both ways: the megatrend is real, but its returns
are unevenly distributed and have historically flowed to the suppliers of scarce key
technology rather than to the car brands. Thematic ETFs launched near peak
sentiment have lost roughly 30 per cent in risk-adjusted terms over their first five
years. Whoever wants to take part therefore diversifies across the value chain,
weights platform and technology leaders above hopeful newcomers, avoids naming
small specialists, and measures success in decades, not quarters.

detail.title: Injunction Frameworks and the Licensing of Standard-Essential Patents

publicationDetails.detailsText: ZEW – Centre for European Economic Research Discussion Paper No. 26-038

detail.abstract: We develop a licensing-litigation model to analyze how different injunction frameworks affect bargaining behavior, equilibrium royalties, and litigation outcomes in standard-essential patent (SEP) disputes. Motivated by recent developments in German case law, we compare two legal frameworks that differ only in whether the patent holder's licensing offer conditions the availability of injunctive relief. We show that removing the patent holder's offer from the injunction analysis raises equilibrium royalties and the risk of patent holdup when courts are sufficiently imprecise in assessing FRAND compliance; when courts are predictable, the two frameworks coincide. Higher royalties arise because SEP holders make more aggressive, non-FRAND, licensing offers, while implementers respond with higher counteroffers to reduce the risk of an injunction. The same mechanism, however, can reduce the incidence of injunctions, so injunction frequency is an imperfect measure of holdup. Whether the higher royalties raise or lower welfare depends on where the socially optimal royalty lies relative to the rates the two frameworks produce.

detail.abstract: The global food system is projected to experience increasing challenges over the years due to rising population and per capita consumption. Rapid population growth magnifies the effects of climate change by depleting resources and increasing exposure to climate-related risks, especially in urban areas with limited resources. Urban poor people have been proven to be more vulnerable to rising global food issues, climatic changes and unemployment rates due to unique elements of their urban life. Cities that deal with multiple urbanization challenges ultimately develop an urban sprawl which has detrimental effects on the economy, society and environment. Here comes the prevalence of urban agriculture as a form of modern agriculture that places an emphasis on its numerous goals in ensuring food security, maintaining urban ecosystem services and enhancing urban living standards. Urban green spaces are universally acknowledged as a nature-based solution that promotes social cohesion, healthy living and climate change mitigation and adaptation. Urban agriculture benefits a community in a variety of ways, from providing food and nutritional security, economic and environmental benefits and even modifying a city's urban form.

detail.abstract: We develop a dynamic equilibrium model of a tokenized platform with endogenous decentralized verification. The framework distinguishes miners, who incur mining costs to validate transactions, from non-mining participants, who hold tokens only for transactional benefits. Competition and subsidy-financed mining rewards generate a dual regime: with a small miner base, rents attract all entrants into mining; with a large base, rent dissipation channels entry toward non-mining participation. The model predicts a doubleS shaped adoption trajectory and a discrete upward shift in user-base volatility at the switching point. Using on-chain data, we find robust empirical support that the miner base is the primary fundamental determinant of token adoption and valuation.

detail.abstract: Conditional-moment estimation and dynamic portfolio choice complement each other. Our results support this complementarity in high-dimensional multiperiod problems with transaction costs and constraints. We estimate policies from intertemporal optimality restrictions. An Adversarial Intertemporal Moment (AIM) estimator learns conditional test functions that uncover predictable violations, while a recurrent policy adapts to evolving states. The losscomparison test provides evidence against multiperiod optimality of the myopic policy at every multiperiod horizon. Over a twelve-month investment horizon, the AIM-estimated dynamic policy achieves a 25.7% annualized certaintyequivalent return in out-of-sample results of U.S. equities, compared with 12.1% for its myopic counterpart.

detail.abstract: A frictionless view holds that intermediaries do not affect asset prices because households alone determine valuations. A simple model of delegation shows instead that prices reflect a weighted average of households' and intermediaries' subjective beliefs, with household influence determined by delegation strength, risk attitudes, and intermediaries' regulatory and contractual incentives. We use investor surveys to recover household influence as a time-varying latent process. We reject the frictionless view even in the stock market, arguably the least intermediated major asset class, while showing that the growth of intermediation substantially overstates the dilution of household influence. We link fluctuations in influence to risk, financial constraints, and the regulatory and technological forces reshaping US markets.

title: Sterilized FX Intervention and Exchange Rate Stability

detail.title: Sterilized FX Intervention and Exchange Rate Stability

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, human data, or animals, and therefore did not require ethics committee approval.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether sterilized central bank intervention reliably stabilizes exchange rates, challenging the assumption embedded in much of the policy literature. Using evidence from both advanced and emerging market economies, we show that sterilized intervention's effectiveness is conditional rather than universal. Three channels-portfolio balance, signaling, and coordination-are theorized to transmit intervention to exchange rates, but their strength varies with market conditions, capital account openness, and the credibility of the intervening authority. A comparative analysis of seven intervention episodes indicates that sterilized intervention can reduce short-term volatility and lean against disorderly market conditions, but it rarely reverses fundamentals-driven trends and can even destabilize rates when it conflicts with market expectations or signals policy inconsistency. Intervention is most effective when it is unexpected, coordinated across central banks, and accompanied by consistent monetary policy signals; it is least effective in thin markets, under sustained one-way pressure, or when perceived as resisting fundamentals. These findings suggest that sterilized intervention should be understood as a tool for smoothing volatility under specific conditions rather than a guaranteed mechanism for exchange rate stabilization.

title: The Global Maximum Point Invariance Theorem: A Statistical Invariant Theory of Structural Break Detection — Unified Shape Function, Standardized Limits, and Multi-regime Generalization

detail.title: The Global Maximum Point Invariance Theorem: A Statistical Invariant Theory of Structural Break Detection — Unified Shape Function, Standardized Limits, and Multi-regime Generalization

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No competing interests
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding

detail.abstract: This paper establishes a mathematical theorem system for between-group regression difference statistics in structural break detection. The central result is the Global Maximum Point Invariance Theorem: in a two-regime linear switching model with homogeneous second-moment design, with fixed noise variance σ² > 0, under the standardized limit as n → ∞, the standardized limits of Chow F/n, Wald/n, and LR/n all attain their global unique maximum at the true regime boundary. On both sides of the true boundary, the standardized limits of the three statistics are strictly increasing functions of a common unified shape function h(τ)—Wald/n shares the same form as Chow F/n up to a factor of the constant p, while LR/n is another nonlinear monotone transformation; if the distribution of the regime variable T is symmetric about the true boundary, the three can be merged into a globally single-valued strictly monotone function of h(τ). This invariance property is derived rigorously from two independent facts: convex combination geometry and statistical algebra. Under fixed σ² > 0, the paper establishes a non-asymptotic shrinkage bound: the estimated coefficients at an incorrectly split point converge to the mixed coefficient at rate n^(−1/2), and the upper bound holds for every fixed candidate threshold; a corollary further demonstrates that in finite samples, the statistic value at any incorrectly split point is suppressed below the value at the true boundary with high probability. The paper proves a multi-regime global optimality theorem: BIC attains its global minimum at the true set of regime boundaries, with complete proofs covering underfitting, overfitting, and mislocation. It also establishes a switching intensity monotonicity theorem and an initial parameter–position–difference-vector identifiability proposition. Furthermore, the paper formulates the relaxation of A3 as a generalized regime mixing lemma, proving that when the discrepancy between the second moments of the design matrices in the two regimes tends to zero, the peak location offset is O(‖Σ₁ − Σ₂‖); through a slow-variation robustness proposition for the cusp structure, it further proves that when the in-regime parameter vector varies slowly at a rate below a critical threshold, the maximum point of the statistic does not shift. The Onsager–Yang exact solution of the 2D Ising model verifies the slow-variation robustness proposition—the Chow F peak precisely locks onto T_c = 2.269185; the intercept/slope ratio is strictly monotone in the distance from T_c (ρ = 1.0000), providing cross-disciplinary support for the switching intensity monotonicity theorem. This paper establishes a unified mathematical framework for the consistency of the maximum points of between-group regression difference statistics in structural break detection.

title: The Nexus of Entrepreneurship and Credit Market: A Tale of Two Frictions

detail.abstract: This paper studies endogenous entrepreneurship and bank credit supply when adverse selection in entrepreneurial entry interacts with moral hazard in loan repayment. Individuals differ in entrepreneurial ability and rely on unsecured bank credit upon entry. Because banks cannot observe borrower quality or outside opportunities, they offer a common borrowing limit to maximize its expected profit. Greater outside-option dispersion discourages high-ability agents from entering entrepreneurship while encouraging low-ability agents to enter, thereby worsening borrower composition and increasing default risk. The resulting credit response is non-monotonic: banks expand credit when dispersion is moderate but tighten credit once adverse selection becomes sufficiently severe. Because entrepreneurs take the common borrowing limit as given, they do not internalize how their entry and default decisions affect borrower composition and bank lendings, generating a credit-market externality. Comparing the decentralized equilibrium with a constrained-efficient allocation shows that laissez-faire credit can be inefficiently low. Policy effects depend on how interventions affect entrepreneurship, repayment incentives, and bank lending. Entry-cost subsidies can worsen borrower composition and contract credit, moderate default guarantees can relax credit constraints, while interest subsidies targeted at repaying borrowers improve both entry quality and repayment incentives. A calibrated dynamic extension confirms the non-monotonic responses of credit and aggregate output.

title: The Generalized Alpha Log-power Transformed Family: Flexible Tail Behaviour, Statistical Properties and Applications

detail.abstract: This study introduces the Generalized Alpha Log-Power Transformed-G (GALPTG) family, an extension of the Alpha Log-Power Transformed-G framework obtained by introducing two additional shape parameters α and β to provide greater control over distributional shape and tail behaviour. A particular member, the Generalized Alpha Log-Power Transformed Log-Logistic (GALPTL-LoG) distribution, is developed using the log-logistic distribution as the baseline model. A key theoretical property of the proposed model is its flexible asymptotic right-tail behaviour. While the log-logistic baseline has a regularly varying survival function with tail exponent θ, the GALPTLLoG distribution has tail exponent θ(-log β). Several statistical properties of the proposed family are derived, including linear representations, moments, and moment generating function. Model parameters are estimated using several estimation methods, and their finite-sample performance is assessed through Monte Carlo simulations. Applications to two computing-system reliability datasets involving memory failure and processor lifetimes demonstrate that the GALPTL-LoG distribution consistently outperforms the competing models considered, yielding the most favourable values across all goodness-of-fit measures, including-2 log L, AIC, AICC, BIC, W * , A * , K-S statistic, and K-S p-value. Overall, the theoretical and empirical findings demonstrate the usefulness of the GALPTG family for modelling data exhibiting skewness, complex hazard structures, and varying degrees of right-tail heaviness.

title: Switching Degree: An Axiomatic Effect Size for Structural Break Detection — Axiomatic Foundation, Inference Theory, Power Analysis, and Switching Coupling Decomposition of Regime-switch Metrics

detail.title: Switching Degree: An Axiomatic Effect Size for Structural Break Detection — Axiomatic Foundation, Inference Theory, Power Analysis, and Switching Coupling Decomposition of Regime-switch Metrics

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes the Switching Degree—a standardized effect size that measures “how large a regime switch is” in structural break detection—and establishes its complete axiomatic foundation, inference theory, and power analysis. The Switching Degree is defined as S = ‖Δθ‖_Σ / ‖θ_ref‖_Σ, where ‖·‖_Σ is the Mahalanobis norm induced by the second-moment matrix Σ of the design, a choice that makes the Switching Degree strictly consistent with the unified shape function h(τ) of Tang (2026af): S = √h(τ*) / ‖θ_ref‖_Σ. The paper explicitly distinguishes two complementary effect sizes: the local switching degree S (standardized by a domain-specific reference vector, suitable for within-domain comparisons) and the global effect size S_eff = ‖Δθ‖_Σ / σ (standardized by the noise scale, suitable for cross-disciplinary comparisons and power analysis), and establishes the equivalence relation f² = γ(1−γ)S_eff² linking both to Cohen's f². At the axiomatic level, the paper establishes that, given the data-driven inner-product structure Σ, a switching measure satisfying four natural norm axioms—non-negativity, positive homogeneity, triangle inequality, and the parallelogram law—together with one normalization condition is uniquely the Mahalanobis norm ratio; the role of the parallelogram law is to select the Euclidean norm from among all L^p norms. At the level of inference theory, Theorem F establishes consistency; Theorem G establishes √n(Ŝ−S) → N(0, σ²/[γ(1−γ)‖θ_ref‖_Σ²]); Theorem H provides a non-asymptotic shrinkage bound; Theorem I extends inference to the unknown-boundary setting, deriving the two-sided first-order bias expansion Ŝ_plug − S = −ηS + o_p(n^(−1/2)) and showing that boundary estimation error in either direction leads to systematic underestimation; Theorem J extends inference to the multi-regime setting, deriving the joint asymptotic normality of the switching degree vector Ŝ with a tridiagonal covariance matrix whose off-diagonal entries contain direction-cosine factors; Theorem K provides heteroskedasticity-robust variance corrections and plug-in estimators. Theorem D (Structural Invariance Theorem) proves that the Switching Degree is invariant under invertible Σ-isometries. The paper further introduces the switching coupling degree and proves Theorem C (Switching Degree Decomposition Theorem): the squared path switching degree equals the squared net switching degree plus the squared coupling switching degree; in the one-dimensional case, the relation between the switching coupling degree and mutual information is I(Δθ₁; Δθ₂) = −(1/2)log(1−cos²φ). The 2D Ising model provides numerical verification at the Onsager-calibrated critical temperature (S = 0.5, S_eff ≈ 25.8). Numerical simulations verify the finite-sample behavior of the inference theory and report a negative result: with unknown boundaries, the switching degree estimator exhibits a systematic negative bias (bias approximately 81% of the theoretical standard error), and residual bootstrap quantile intervals raise coverage only from 84.5% to 86.5%, far below the nominal 95%—demonstrating that post-selection bias is a substantive first-order problem that naive bootstrap cannot correct and that explicit corrections such as conditional bias expansion are required.

title: Between Countries, not within: Family Policy and the Intergenerational Transmission of Disadvantage in Europe

detail.title: Between Countries, not within: Family Policy and the Intergenerational Transmission of Disadvantage in Europe

detail.abstract: Cross-national research consistently finds that European countries with more generous family policy exhibit weaker intergenerational transmission of economic disadvantage. This paper asks whether that regularity reflects a policy effect or a country effect. Using harmonised Eurostat data on the retrospective childhood circumstances of adults aged 25-59, combined with OECD family-policy series reaching back to 1980, the analysis proceeds in two stages. Across countries, the association is strong and robust: a onepercentage-point increase in family-benefit spending as a share of GDP is associated with a 2.2-3.8 percentage-point narrowing of the childhood-origin poverty gap, a result that survives controls for national income and unemployment, reproduces across two independent classifiers of childhood disadvantage, and does not change sign in any leave-one-country-out iteration. Within countries, across birth cohorts exposed to different policy regimes during childhood, the same association is a precisely estimated zero; the confidence interval excludes effects larger than roughly one-sixth of the cross-national estimate. A placebo test shows why: family-policy generosity is so persistent within countries that childhood and adult exposure windows correlate at 0.83, leaving too little cohort-specific variation to identify a timing effect. The paper concludes that the cross-national gradient is a between-country institutional regularity rather than demonstrated evidence of a policy mechanism, and documents two measurement pitfalls encountered along the way.

title: The Difficulty of Telling Signal from Noise when Noise Lingers

detail.abstract: How many observations does it take to detect a fixed signal when the noise has long memory? For a sample-mean detector applied to a constant signal buried in fractionally integrated noise of order d ∈ [0, 1/2), I give a closed-form expression for the sample size required to reach a target power at a fixed size: T q (d) = [(τ + Φ-1 (q)) σ √ c d /(δx)] 2/(1-2d). The exponent 2/(1-2d) is the whole story: the required sample size is a power function of detection difficulty whose exponent diverges as d → 1/2. A doubling of detection difficulty that costs four times the data under independence costs 2 10 times the data at d = 0.4. A Monte Carlo confirms the formula delivers the target power and size.
