detail.abstract: Autonomous pricing agents transact against one another at machine speed in perishable-inventory markets. The governance layer meant to restrain them is still written as software intent, and software intent is a property of whichever model happens to hold it, so enforcement weakens precisely as counterparty capability strengthens. We remove that dependence. Four tiers: AKIF gates inbound market state on type, provenance and range; BVEF converts resource stocks into a biophysical occupancy ceiling 𝐹 𝑏𝑖𝑜 ; the Detektor-Safe Harness runs a CUSUM filter over cross-agent rate correlation; a YEP kernel composes all three into a single rate floor 𝜔. That floor is sealed inside a hardware-isolated enclave ℰ 𝑒𝑛𝑐𝑙𝑎𝑣𝑒 at attestation, after which no write path to it exists. Proposition 1 establishes that attainable violation of 𝜔 is constant in adversary capability 𝜅. The argument is short. Capability enters only through the proposal argument of a monotone operator whose infimum over the entire policy function space is already 𝜔. A 237-key resort calibration moves fifth-percentile net operating income from-0.179M to +0.901M USD and cuts the probability of negative NOI from 6.14 per cent to 0.01 per cent. What remains is physical risk, not computational risk.

detail.abstract: An AI system may produce useful drafts, classifications, recommendations, or reconciliations while an organization remains unable to delegate the operative decision. Traceability may be inadequate, sign-off non-delegable, authority boundaries unclear, the audit trail incomplete, or accountability unacceptable. CELLTheory,ConstrainedEndosymbioticLeadership &Logistics, addresses this problem as a function level governance model. Its core contribution is a constrained model of residual decision-authority allo cation; CELL supplies the architecture and vocabulary used to operationalize it. The model first applies categorical reservations and non-compensatory traceability and legitimacy floors within the VITAL as sessment of Viability, Integration, Traceability, Autonomy, and Legitimacy. Feasible assignments then compare the approved human process with recurring AI cost plus expected governance loss. Separate components characterize compute scaling and a Compliance Antibody Registry, defined as validated, retrievable control-memory rather than raw logging. The biological labels are mnemonics mapped to ob servable corporate objects and formal terms, not evidence that firms behave like cells. Three constructed sector cases illustrate the allocation rule; they are not observed cases or empirical tests. Validation is prospective and requires firm-function-period data capable of distinguishing prediction, within-function association, causal identification, and structural calibration. The analysis stops at function-level gover nance allocation; valuation and aggregate economic consequences require separate models and data.

detail.title: The Cost of Regard: Interpersonal Attention as a Choice, and the Budget as a First-Order Condition

detail.abstract: Models of social preference constrain the weights an individual places on the payoffs of others to sum to a constant. A companion paper isolated that constraint as an axiom on preference — population invariance of the attention budget — and supplied the elicitation that tests it; what it did not supply is a reason the axiom should hold, or a theory of what its failure would measure. This paper supplies both by making attention a choice. An individual facing payoff-relevant others allocates costly attention across them; the weight the elicitation recovers is attended stake, w_ij = a_j·s_j; and the budget solves a first-order condition equating the marginal value of vigilance to the marginal cost of attention. Three results follow. First, the optimal allocation is a threshold rule: others whose importance falls below the shadow price of attention receive exactly zero weight, so the unresented party of the conflict series is a corner solution rather than a definition, and a rise in one rival's importance crowds bystanders out — conflict manufactures unresented parties. Second, the shape of the budget in the group size is the shape of the attention cost: a linear cost makes the budget proportional to the group, any strictly convex cost makes it increasing and bounded with log-elasticity ρ = Λ/(Λ + m·C''), and exact invariance — the axiom of the literature — holds if and only if the marginal cost of attention is perfectly inelastic, a hard capacity, in which case the divisor 1/(n−1) emerges as the shadow of the binding constraint. The normalization of Fehr–Schmidt and Snidal is thereby identified as the hypothesis that attention is supplied along a vertical curve, and the curvature of the budget across group sizes, measurable by the companion paper's single indifference repeated at three sizes, becomes an estimate of the elasticity of the marginal cost of attention. Third, in the dyad the spite parameter of the Product Theorem becomes an equilibrium object, λ = a·s: war raises the stake and attention follows, so the feasibility condition λ_R·λ_U ≤ 1 depends on a history that the parameter itself created, and a bistable region exists in which war and peace are each self-sustaining. Policy operates on stakes and on the price of attention; no lever operates on preferences directly, because the preference is downstream.

detail.abstract: Emerging-market joint ventures (JVs) frequently rely on foreign technology to navigate institutional voids-regulatory ambiguity, fragmented supply chains, and infrastructure deficits-yet many struggle to convert this knowledge into global export capability. Prior research typically models foreign technology licencing, internal R&D, and external search as discrete, additive inputs; we instead conceptualise them as an interdependent configuration. We ask how JVs recombine these heterogeneous knowledge sources to build export capability under resource scarcity. Using an abductive, longitudinal process-tracing design across ten legal entities in eight Indian manufacturing and life-science contexts (FY2015-FY2025), we prioritise audited statutory and regulatory disclosures to mitigate self-reporting bias. We find that successful JVs follow a sequential process-then-product pathway whose ordering is dictated by resource scarcity. We refine absorptive capacity theory by showing that realised absorptive capacity functions as a threshold condition rather than a continuous, linear moderator. Below this critical capability floor, foreign licencing deepens technological dependence; above it, JVs configure inbound open innovation as an active institutional buffer, transforming domestic compliance constraints into scalable export capabilities. Export readiness thus depends less on the raw volume of innovation inputs than on the architectural alignment of local R&D and technical governance.

detail.abstract: The island of Ireland, due to the weight of patriarchal worldbuilding, is a font of feminist legal practice. But the habitual story of resistance to domination, while true, often overshadows another tale, which places feminist practice from across the island at its heart. Using the mythical island of Hy-Brasil as a site of mirror feminist worldbuilding, this Foreword centres the innovative and imaginative feminist praxis of the past and present to bring to the fore the font of feminist legal practice that exists and to advocate for a new way of doing both law and the law school. The Foreword uses backcasting as its primary method incorporating pre-figuration, critical utopian worldbuilding and (anti)hagiographies through texts and figures that are often not regarded as part of the Irish legal canon. In a feminist mode of academic writing that eschews claims of objectivity or rationality it offers a personal account of Irish legal feminism. The Foreword argues that the island of Ireland/Hy-Brasil embodies feminist jurisdictional innovation, which should overshadow its other legal legacies.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) use in the European Union is increasing rapidly, yet adoption remains uneven across Member States, sectors and population groups. While data show growing exposure to AI in households and enterprises, a significant share of Europeans still perceive no need to use AI. This paper argues that this gap cannot be explained by technology or regulation alone, but must be understood as a strategic communication and sense-making challenge. Drawing on Eurostat and Eurobarometer data, the Stanford AI Index and a practice-based case involving women entrepreneurs and youth participants in financial literacy education, the paper examines how deterrence-based narratives (cheating, risk, compliance) limit engagement, while human-first, competence-oriented communication fosters trust, relevance and ethical use. Across both participant groups, initial framings of AI as a threat to integrity gave way, following a narrative reframing intervention, to conditional trust and responsibility-based ethical reasoning. The study contributes to communication management scholarship by positioning communication framing as a key determinant of AI legitimacy, trust and adoption in the EU context, and by identifying strategic communication as a mediating mechanism between AI governance and stakeholder outcomes.

detail.abstract: We study how mass-layoff announcements affect electoral outcomes using a newly assembled dataset of US establishment-level administrative notices from the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Act. A matched event study compares same-state counties with and without sizable WARN-announced layoffs. Controlling for local labor-market conditions, layoff announcements increase the Democratic-Republican vote margin by reducing Republican votes and increasing Democratic votes without clearly altering election winners or incumbent support. Effects appear across political offices, are not driven by manufacturing decline, and are geographically localized. The responses operate through turnout composition rather than vote switching and result in no policy-induced changes in transfer payments.

title: Four Forecasts, One Word: Optimality Criteria, Their Incompatibilities, and the Governance of Prediction in Organizations

detail.title: Four Forecasts, One Word: Optimality Criteria, Their Incompatibilities, and the Governance of Prediction in Organizations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare the following financial interests/ personal relationships which may be considered as potential competing interests: Harrison Katz reports a relationship with Airbnb that includes: employment.
declarations.funderStatement: The author received no external funding.

detail.abstract: The word "forecast" routinely names a single artifact, yet organizations ask it to do four jobs: to estimate the future state of the world, to set a plan they commit and resource against, to serve as the scorecard performance is judged by, and to act as a signal that moves resources before the outcome is known. This paper argues that the four jobs carry four distinct optimality criteria and that the criteria stand in a definite structure, which it states as four propositions. The estimate is the only non derived object. The scorecard is a frozen, adjudicated vintage of it. The plan and the signal are derived artifacts that diverge from the estimate, the plan through a loss functional the forecaster chooses and can name, the signal through an audience reaction the forecaster can only bound. On this account, a central and underappreciated forecasting failure in organizations is not low accuracy but the collapse of these four objects into a single artifact, which converts a design problem into recurring conflict. Because all four criteria are conditional on a stable information regime, the paper identifies a decomposition layer, one that separates intervention effects, regime effects, and residual forecast error, as the requirement that keeps the structure intact under non stationarity. It closes with implications for forecast governance and organizational design.

detail.abstract:
Before a public–private partnership (PPP) delivers a kilometre of road or a day of hospital care, a prior question is settled — usually without the Ministry of Finance in the room: does the contract count as government debt? The answer is not economic but statistical and accounting: it depends on which rule book scores the deal and how the contract allocates risk on paper. And it moves the one number a fiscal rule watches.
This paper is the keystone of the Austral series because it derives the "silent liability" the other papers
price. A PPP is silent not because its cost is unknowable but because the recognition rule lets it sit off
the recorded stock. Three live rule books answer the recognition question and they disagree byconstruction: the European statistical standard ESA 2010 (with the Eurostat Manual on Government
Deficit and Debt) records a PPP off the government balance sheet whenever the private partner bears
construction risk and at least one of availability or demand risk; the accounting standard IPSAS 32
(the public-sector mirror of IFRIC 12) recognises the asset and liability whenever the grantor controls
the service and the residual interest — a test most PPPs meet; and the IMF's GFSM 2014 follows
economic ownership. The same contract can therefore be off the statistical balance sheet, on the
accounting one, and economically sovereign regardless. The United Kingdom's Private Finance Initiative
is the textbook case: under IFRS/IFRIC 12 (adopted for central government from 2009-10) nearly all
PFI sits on the Whole of Government Accounts, yet under ESA/National Accounts the majority stayed
off headline Public Sector Net Debt — the Office for Budget Responsibility put the off-balance-sheet PFI
stock at roughly £35 billion, about 2.5% of GDP, at March 2010.
The disagreement has a second layer that is the heart of the matter: the statistical rule is only as good
as the jurisdiction that applies it. The European rule is strict — under the EPEC–Eurostat 2016 Guide
to the Statistical Treatment of PPPs, any minimum-revenue or minimum-demand guarantee puts the PPP
on the government balance sheet, and Portugal's 2010 reclassification of road PPPs into general
government shows the rule has teeth. But ESA is European; most of the world's PPPs sit under GFSM
2014, IPSAS, or no binding standard at all — Chile and the emerging markets this series addresses
— where that strict guarantee rule is not applied, so the same minimum-revenue guarantee lands off
the binding debt measure and is disclosed, if at all, only as a contingent liability. The recognition gap is
therefore jurisdiction-dependent: it is widest exactly where the rule is weakest.
The contribution is a reproducible cross-framework recognition scorer: feed a contract's risk-
allocation matrix and it returns the on/off classification under all four lenses and computes the
recognition gap — the value off the jurisdiction's binding statistical measure yet economically
sovereign — for the strict (EU/ESA) and the loose (non-EU/GFSM) regime alike. On three worked
contracts the gap is legible: an availability hospital off under the statistical rule but on under IPSAS
(the UK-PFI divergence, present in every jurisdiction); a demand-risk toll road with a minimum-revenue
guarantee that the EU rule catches but a GFSM/IPSAS jurisdiction does not, so its gap appears only
outside the EU; and a government-funded social asset the majority-financing test pulls on the books
everywhere. The portfolio recognition gap is 1.2% of GDP under the strict EU rule and 1.8% under
the looser non-EU regime — the same contracts, a larger hidden liability where the rule is weaker.
The policy lead follows: adopt the strict treatment of guarantees (catch the minimum-revenue
guarantee on the balance sheet, as the EU does), disclose the recognition gap alongside the rule-
relevant treatment, cap the off-balance-sheet stock, and pre-commit the classification at tender.

detail.abstract: This paper estimates the causal effect of extractive natural resource rents on income leakage in Sub-Saharan Africa. keywords: Economic Pressure to Invest in Worker Cooling

detail.abstract:
Occupational heat stress has rapidly shifted from a peripheral safety concern to a central regulatory and industrial‑strategy variable across tropical and rapidly industrializing economies. As the report notes, “2.4 billion workers – 70.9% of the global workforce – now face exposure to excessive heat on the job” and heat already causes “18,970 deaths and 22.87 million injuries annually” . By 2030, the International Labour Organization projects that heat stress will erase 2.2% of global working hours, equivalent to 80 million full‑time jobs and US$2.4 trillion in output losses, with agriculture and construction absorbing 79% of the burden .

The report argues that four forces—mandatory rest-period regulation, productivity‑loss quantification, employer‑liability expansion, and the economics of cooling investment—are converging into a single strategic pressure shaping labor markets, supply chains, and capital allocation. This pressure is formalized in the 4M Framework (Mandate, Measure, Mitigate, Mobilize), which explains how regulatory thresholds, actuarial data, and legal exposure translate into rising investment in cooling infrastructure. As stated, “liability exposure—more than the regulations themselves—is now the primary driver pushing capital toward cooling infrastructure” .

Using the Compound Vulnerability Multiplier (D‑Coefficient × P‑Integral × Exposure Density), the report shows why similar physical heat exposure produces divergent outcomes across jurisdictions. High‑capacity states like Qatar convert extreme heat into enforceable compliance regimes, while countries such as India and Vietnam face rising exposure without codified statutory protection. Meanwhile, California demonstrates how litigation and workers’‑compensation records can substitute for federal regulation, generating a de facto liability‑driven investment model.

Across converging tropical economies, the report concludes that occupational heat stress is no longer a discrete safety issue but a structural determinant of competitiveness, shaping where firms locate production, how governments design labor codes, and how investors price operational risk. The economies that successfully sequence Mandate → Measure → Mitigate → Mobilize will be best positioned to convert rising heat exposure into regulatory stability, industrial resilience, and long‑term economic advantage.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between financial literacy and household savings behaviour in developing economies, with particular reference to India. Drawing on a review of existing empirical literature, survey data from prior studies, and primary observations gathered through financial literacy workshops conducted with over 250 participants in Surat, India, the paper argues that financial literacy is a significant and independent determinant of savings behaviour, operating through multiple channels including reduced present bias, increased engagement with formal financial systems, and improved long-term planning capacity. The paper identifies a structural gap between urban and rural financial literacy rates in India, documents the persistence of informal savings mechanisms among low-literacy households, and examines how behavioural biases amplify the consequences of financial ignorance. The paper further analyses the limitations of existing financial education interventions and proposes a framework for understanding the conditions under which literacy improvements translate into durable changes in savings behaviour. The findings carry implications for policy design in economies where household savings rates are both economically critical and structurally inadequate.

detail.abstract:
This report separates antisemitism into three units of analysis that answer different questions: the person, the organization, and the political actor. The sibling report, Antisemitism as Political Technology, covers the third level, a political charge deployed to acquire or hold power. This report supplies the two accounts that report excludes by design: individual prejudice and organizational-institutional discrimination. No level reduces to another. A private citizen can
hold anti-Jewish beliefs with no political actor involved; an organization can keep excluding
Jews after the people who wrote the exclusionary rule are gone; a politician can deploy an
antisemitic charge without believing it. The levels interact through documented mechanisms,
but the interactions do not collapse the distinction (Section 0).

title: How to Define Financial Performance
affiliations: INSEAD

detail.title: How to Define Financial Performance
detail.abstract: For several decades, rent has served as the theoretical dependent variable of strategy. Empirically however, performance has been operationalized using many different measures that do not capture the concept of economic rents. More fundamentally, common rent definitions are based on equilibrium assumptions that are untenable in most contemporary market conditions. To address this situation, this study proposes to replace rent with the concept of "fully-loaded profit", a measure of ex post net present value. It is this measure that managers are supposed to optimize. The study offers a formal analysis fully-loaded profit's properties. These properties are used to derive three new performance measures to be used in empirical studies: adjusted economic profit (AEP), market-based economic profit (MEP), and adjusted market-based economic profit (AMEP).

detail.abstract:
The RUU Migas 2026, now a DPR initiative bill, is Indonesia's attempt to repair a fteen-
year statutory vacuum in oil-and-gas governance created by two Constitutional Court rulings.
This paper asks the question TEMPO poses: does the substance now on oer actually answer
the sector's fundamental problemsin governance, institutions, investment, production, and
public interest (the Energy Trilemma)or does it introduce new risks? We combine the
IRCGE model, which prices what is measurable in general equilibrium (scal balance, welfare,
distribution, carbon, the sovereign-fund dynamics), with a regulatory-gap analysis for what
the model cannot price (the regulatoroperator fusion, contract sanctity, governance quality).
The central nding is that the bill answers today's scal problem well but under-
answers the intergenerational and securityclimate problems, and each shortfall is
addressable with a specic, quantied amendment. Pricing reform turns a net oil-and-gas
scal balance heading to −Rp 70 tn (−US$ 3.5 bn) into +Rp 96 tn (+US$ 4.9 bn) by 2035
while cutting the largest deadweight loss and leaving the income distribution essentially
unchanged. But the bill's Petroleum Fund is designed as a drilling fund, not a savings
fund: a genuine institution would accumulate Rp 4,591 tn (US$ 233 bn) by 2035 and raise
present-day GDP and consumption. Neither the 2026 nor the 2018 draft closes the security
or climate gapsimport dependence still climbs to ∼42% and CO2 to ∼652 Mtand the

detail.abstract: This study examines the effect of behavioral biases and the moderating effect of financial literacy on financial performance of SMEs in Afghanistan. This study adopted quantitative research design and primary data were collected from 300 SMEs in three provinces of Afghanistan namely Nangarhar, Helmand and Khost through structured questionnaire. The study employed exploratory factor analysis (EFA), correlation analysis, multiple regression and hierarchical regression to establish the effect of biases on the financial performance of SMEs. The study results indicated that overconfidence bias has a significant positive relationship with the financial performance of SMEs while the anchoring effect bias, herding behavior bias and the loss aversion has a significant negative relationship with the financial performance of SMEs. Among these, loss aversion was most strongly related to financial performance. The regression result also suggested that financial literacy has a significant impact in reducing the relationship between behavioral biases and financial performance. That is, it reduces the negative impact of behavioral biases. This study is one of the first to apply the concepts of behavioral finance to a fragile post-conflict setting and offers some suggestions for policy makers, financial institutions and business owners to improve the performance of SMEs by enhancing the financial literacy and awareness of their stakeholders.

detail.title: Digital Transformation Capabilities and Supply Chain Finance Resilience: An Integrated AI-Blockchain-analytics Framework

detail.abstract:
Supply chain finance (SCF) plays a pivotal role in maintaining liquidity and operational continuity across global value networks. However, systemic supply chain disruptions, macroeconomic volatility, and information asymmetry frequently expose SCF programs to severe friction and default risks. While digital transformation is widely touted as a catalyst for supply chain resilience, empirical evidence regarding the explicit mechanisms through which distinct digital transformation capabilities enhance Supply Chain Finance Resilience (SCFR) remains fragmented. Grounded in the Resource-Based View (RBV), Dynamic Capabilities Theory (DCT), and Information Processing Theory (IPT), this study develops and tests an integrated framework evaluating the direct and indirect impacts of Artificial Intelligence Capability (AIC), Blockchain Capability (BC), and Data Analytics Capability (DAC) on SCFR, mediated by Digital Trust in SCF Platforms (DT). 

Using a computational research simulation methodology, a respondent-level dataset (𝑁 = 500) representing supply chain, finance, operations, and IT decision-makers across international enterprises was algorithmically generated under a defensible latent-variable covariance structure. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with 5,000 bootstrap resamples was executed to evaluate the measurement and structural models. The structural analysis reveals that AIC (𝛽 = 0.241, 𝑝 < .001), BC (𝛽 = 0.312, 𝑝 < .001), and DAC (𝛽 = 0.284, 𝑝 < .001) significantly and positively drive Digital Trust in SCF Platforms, explaining 54.2% of its variance (𝑅 2 = 0.542). Digital Trust, in turn, exerts a substantial direct effect on SCFR (𝛽 = 0.385, 𝑝 < .001). Furthermore, direct effects on SCFR were confirmed for DAC (𝛽 = 0.218, 𝑝 < .001) and AIC (𝛽 = 0.152, 𝑝 = .002), whereas the direct link from BC to SCFR was non-significant (𝛽 = 0.071, 𝑝 = .158). Formal mediation testing using percentile bootstrapping confirmed that Digital Trust fully mediates the relationship between Blockchain Capability and SCFR, while partially mediating the relationships for AIC and DAC. The overall structural model accounts for 58.6% of the variance in Supply Chain Finance Resilience (𝑅 2 = 0.586, 𝑄 predict 2 = 0.412). 

This methodological prototype advances theoretical understanding by unpacking the granular capability configurations necessary to foster digital trust and financial resilience in supply networks. For practitioners and policymakers, the findings highlight that investing in blockchain technology yields minimal resilience benefits unless coupled with platform-wide digital trust mechanisms, whereas AI and analytics offer dual-pathway benefits across operational and relational domains.

title: A Layered Manufacturing Intelligence Platform Integrating Ontologies, Knowledge Graphs, Predictive Analytics, and Autonomous Agents for Intelligent Factory Operations

detail.abstract:
The increasing complexity of discrete and continuous manufacturing operations demands intelligent
information architectures that transcend conventional supervisory control systems. This paper
presents a comprehensive conceptual framework for a seven-layer Manufacturing Intelligence
Platform (MIP), integrating ontology-based semantic modelling, knowledge graph entity-relationship
representation, rule-based reasoning, graph-theoretic predictive analytics, large language model
(LLM) natural language generation, AI-assisted decision support, and autonomous agent-driven
operational intervention. Grounded in the ISA-95 (IEC 62264) standard, the proposed architecture
provides a formal semantic foundation for manufacturing data contextualization, enabling
automated inference of equipment risk states, multi-hop genealogy traversal, and real-time anomaly
classification. A graph transformer component learns relational patterns across heterogeneous
manufacturing variables, producing probabilistic forecasts for Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE),
equipment failure risk, and expected downtime with demonstrated predictive accuracy. The LLM
layer translates analytical outputs into verifiable, contextualized natural language narratives, while
the AI assistant tier responds to complex operator queries without autonomous intervention. The
apex AI agent tier executes closed-loop corrective workflows autonomously, encompassing root
cause analysis, work order creation, supervisory notification, intervention scheduling, and post-
action performance monitoring. Through structured architectural analysis and illustrative
instantiation within a plastic injection molding production environment, this paper demonstrates the
mechanism-level pathways by which the MIP architecture reduces operational risk, accelerates
corrective response latency, and enables scalable, data-driven manufacturing intelligence. Future
research directions include ontology-constrained graph neural network training, multi-agent conflict
resolution, cross-enterprise semantic federation, and longitudinal return-on-investment
benchmarking.

detail.abstract: Digital gold platforms promise retail and institutional market participants seamless, fractional access to physical precious metals through modern cryptographic tokens, digital receipts, and web ledgers. However, the legal and operational architecture governing the underlying physical collateral is frequently misunderstood. This working paper examines the structural dichotomy between economic exposure and legal ownership in digital gold platforms. We unpack the three foundational custody models: Allocated Gold (direct proprietary title under bailment), Unallocated Gold (unsecured debtor-creditor claims), and Pooled Gold Interests (fractional equitable co-ownership or tenancy-in-common). By evaluating their legal mechanics, insolvency ring-fencing, rehypothecation dynamics, and vault auditability, we provide an analytical decision matrix for market designers and investors. Finally, we contextualize how next-generation digital gold platformsincluding emerging regional initiatives such as Zelata-can bridge high-frequency retail fractionalization with authentic insolvency-remote asset segregation.

detail.abstract: Research-integrity governance is increasingly performed by a compact trans-organizational field whose participants move among journal editing, publisher oversight, policy development, conference governance, nonprofit watchdogging, authorship and public post-publication criticism. This critical documentary review uses Research Integrity and Peer Review (RIPR) as a longitudinal case through which to examine that architecture. Public records from 2015 to 2026 show that the journal was launched through a partnership between academic editors and BioMed Central’s in-house research-integrity personnel, announced in connection with the World Conference on Research Integrity, and later positioned as a venue for conference proceedings and field-building discussion. Historical and current records also document overlapping roles involving the Committee on Publication Ethics, the World Conferences on Research Integrity Foundation, the Center for Scientific Integrity, publisher integrity functions and RIPR’s editorial structure. None of those facts establishes an improper editorial decision. The problem is narrower and more consequential: the public interface often reveals institutional biographies and reviewer reports without providing a standardized, durable record of handling-editor identity, recusal chronology, substitute-editor independence, title use in external criticism or conflict-sensitive appeal routing. Empirical studies show that editor and reviewer conflict policies are often incomplete, weakly disclosed or inconsistently implemented. This article therefore introduces two analytical concepts—integrity interlock and role portability—and proposes an Integrity-Interlock Disclosure Standard (IIDS). The standard would convert private assurances into auditable metadata while preserving legitimate collaboration and confidentiality. The conclusion is not that integrity experts must withdraw from governance. It is that institutions whose authority rests on transparency should be designed to demonstrate their own independence at the point of decision.

detail.abstract: As a globally popular sport, American football has been exerting an increasingly significant influence. However, the escalating intensity of the game has compelled coaches and players to continuously refine offensive strategies in pursuit of better athletic performance. Given the relative scarcity of research on offensive tactics in the passing plays, this study analyzed a dataset comprising 100 NFL games. Yardage prediction was modeled as a regression problem, while touchdown prediction was modeled as a classification problem. For the regression task, four traditional machine learning models-Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors, XGBoost, and LightGBM-were trained. The best-performing traditional machine learning model was found to be SVM, achieving a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 6.996 yards (lower is better). In comparison, the Llama 3 (8B) large language model fine-tuned with the LoRA method yielded an MAE of 7.059 yards (0.9% larger than that of SVM), performing slightly worse than the best traditional machine learning model. For the classification task, the best traditional machine learning model remained SVM, with a Macro F1 score of 0.614 (higher is better). In contrast, the Llama 3 large model finetuned with the LoRA method achieved a prediction accuracy of 91.1% and Macro F1 score of 0.712 (16.0% higher than that of SVM), significantly outperforming the traditional machine learning models. Based on the findings above, when the number of independent variables is relatively small and the dataset size is limited, traditional machine-learning models are recommended for regression problems. For classification tasks, fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) are preferred. The findings of this study hold substantial practical value in pre-game what-if analyses and theoretical significance regarding the selection of machine learning models for regression and classification tasks.

detail.abstract: This scientific article explores the phenomenon of "cultural diplomacy," examining it as a tool of foreign policy Public Relations (PR) utilized in shaping and consolidating the image of the Russian Federation. The primary objectives of foreign policy PR encompass the creation and enhancement of a positive national image, the advancement of the state's interests, the establishment of trusting and mutually beneficial relations with other nations, and the cultivation of cultural understanding and support from the international community. Acting as a strategic PR instrument, cultural diplomacy plays an indispensable role in the modern world by assisting countries in forging long-term partnerships, advancing intercultural dialogue, and promoting peaceful coexistence within the international arena. This article analyzes how cultural diplomacy facilitates the construction and reinforcement of a state's image, examines this phenomenon through specific empirical examples, and highlights the imperative for the continued existence and evolution of cultural diplomacy initiatives.

title: When Do U.S. Monetary Policy Surprises Matter for Australian Borrowing Costs? Evidence of a Post-2020 Regime Shift

detail.title: When Do U.S. Monetary Policy Surprises Matter for Australian Borrowing Costs? Evidence of a Post-2020 Regime Shift

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no personal, professional, or financial relationships that could have influenced, or could reasonably be perceived to have influenced, this research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The research was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: Does an unanticipated change in U.S. monetary policy raise the yield on Australian Government Securities, and with it the cost of Australian government borrowing? We show that the answer depends critically on when one asks it. Using the high-frequency shock series of Jarociński and Karadi (2020) and Local Projections across the 2-, 5-, and 10-year AGS maturities over 2013-2024, we find the effect is statistically indistinguishable from zero before 2020, and becomes large and reliable only from the COVID period onward-a shift confirmed by a formal structural break test. A surprise comparable to the largest observed in our sample is associated with an increase of approximately eighteen to twenty basis points in Australian yields at impact, operating substantially through co-movement in the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield. These findings indicate that Australian government borrowing costs have grown considerably more exposed to U.S. monetary policy surprises specifically in the post-2020 environment.

title: Data-driven Early Assessment of Energy Performance in Industrial Aluminum Alloy Soaking Furnaces using SCADA Trajectories
affiliations: Central South University, Central South University, Central South University and Central South University

detail.title: Data-driven Early Assessment of Energy Performance in Industrial Aluminum Alloy Soaking Furnaces using SCADA Trajectories
detail.abstract: Industrial aluminum alloy soaking furnaces are long-cycle batch thermal equipment with high energy consumption and delayed availability of final energy-performance indicators. This delay limits timely energy assessment and sustainable operation management during production. This paper proposes a data-driven early assessment method, termed PTEP, for energy performance in industrial soaking furnace operations. The method integrates production-log semantics with early SCADA trajectories describing temperature response, energy evolution, and actuator behavior. Fixed-time windows are constructed for practical early assessment, while proportional windows are used to analyze information gain along batch progress. Regression models estimate final total energy consumption, energy intensity, and soaking stability before batch completion, and classification models identify high-risk batches. Experiments on 385 real production batches from five industrial furnaces show that final total energy consumption can be estimated using only the first 2 h trajectory, achieving an R² of 0.95 and a MAPE of 2.20%. High total-energy-risk batches are identified at the 2 h window with an F1 score of 0.90 and an AUC of 0.98. The proposed method supports early energy-performance assessment and sustainable energy management in long-cycle industrial batch furnaces.

detail.abstract: Firm creation is an essential component of Peruvian productive dynamics; however, its evolution depends on economic and financial conditions that change throughout the cycle. The objective of the study was to determine the influence of business credit, economic activity, business confidence, and financial cost on business creation in Peru during 2012Q1–2025Q4. A quantitative approach, non-experimental and longitudinal design was used, with quarterly secondary data from official sources. The econometric strategy combined descriptive analysis, Hodrick–Prescott filter, unit root tests, identification of structural breakdowns, and an autoregressive model of distributed lags with error correction (ARDL–ECM) and standard Newey–West HAC errors. The results showed a long-term equilibrium relationship and an error correction term of −0.4674 (p = .001), which implies an approximate adjustment of 46.7 % per quarter. Economic activity had the strongest effect: a 1% increase in real GDP was associated with an approximate 1.84% increase in business creation (p = .006). Credit, confidence, interest rates, and inflation did not show robust long-term individual effects. Likewise, the pandemic generated an extraordinary breakthrough, with an estimated 69.8% drop in 2020Q2.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Capacity Control in Sequential Zone Picking Systems
affiliations: University of Duisburg-Essen - Mercator School of Management and University of Duisburg-Essen - Mercator School of Management

detail.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Capacity Control in Sequential Zone Picking Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Nothing to declare.
declarations.funderStatement: None.

detail.abstract: Sequential zone picking systems provide high throughput and flexibility. Under heavy load they are vulnerable to congestion and blocking when conveyor merges, staffing fluctuations, heterogeneous picking speeds, and inventory shortfalls interact. This is especially the case if operations have changing conditions such as changing staffing levels based on throughput targets. Capacity of zone picking systems is commonly regulated using a static pull-based workload mechanism, also referred to as a carton limit that caps the number of boxes in the system. Because this signal is updated only when boxes depart, it can induce oscillatory release behavior and increased recirculation. In this paper we formalize the order release as a binary control problem and introduce a straight forward extension that constrains the number of open picks in the system instead, providing an immediately updated workload measure. Further, we propose a deep reinforcement learning algorithm to control workload mechanisms in zone picking systems dynamically based on the current system state. Our algorithm considers factors such as staffing level, picking speed, and inventory level. We evaluate our static and dynamic approaches in a simulation, where we model a zone picking system from our industry partner HelloFresh, using real-world customer data. Under static, optimal control, the pick limit control increases throughput by up to 2%. A complementary analysis of four months of real-world operational data from a large zone picking system of our industry partner (>100 zones) shows a 6% increase in hourly picks and a 7% reduction in recirculations when pick limit control is applied instead of carton limit control. Our proposed deep reinforcement learning approach achieves an average throughput improvement of approximately 7% relative to a static benchmark. Moreover, in about 8% of the validation instances, it delivers throughput gains of 20% or more.

All data used are publicly available government records (OPM and NCES), and the analysis was conducted independently
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted independently by the author

detail.abstract: Public institutions routinely collect workforce records, yet those records are often used retrospectively rather than as forward-looking signals of capacity risk. This study develops and demonstrates a transparent workforce-capacity methodology using two national administrative data systems: the U.S. Office of Personnel Management's Federal Workforce Data (FWD) platform and the National Center for Education Statistics' Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS). For the EHRI-covered federal civilian workforce, the government-wide hiring-to-separation replacement ratio fell from 1.27 in FY2024 to 0.39 over the trailing twelve months ending May 2026. FY2025 recorded 128,611 retirement-coded separations. After excluding 45,144 retirements flagged under the one-time Deferred Resignation Program, 83,467 non-DRP retirements remained, 28.9 percent above the corrected FY2016-FY2019 pre-pandemic annual baseline of 64,753. Occupational analysis shows that risk is concentrated: several large groups combine very weak replacement with substantial five-year retirement eligibility. In public four-year higher education (N = 827 institutions), verified full-time staff headcount changes from 2018 to 2024 show growth in Business and Financial Operations (+24.0%), Research (+23.4%), and Management (+19.5%), while Office and Administrative Support declined 7.9 percent, or 16,611 positions, even as total staffing increased 7.3 percent. A federal stock-flow retirement model produces a FY2027-FY2030 planning range of 191,344 to 261,910 retirements, with a base scenario of 229,311. The results support a practical conclusion: workforce capacity risk can be detected earlier when replacement, retirement exposure, occupational concentration, and staffing reallocation are monitored together rather than in isolation.

title: Estimating future pandemic harms and gains from preparedness investments
affiliations: Dartmouth College, University of California, Berkeley, Center for Global Development, University of Chicago,  and University of Chicago

detail.title: Estimating future pandemic harms and gains from preparedness investments

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None to declare.
declarations.ethicsApproval: he analysis and conclusions are the authors’ own and not subject to approval by CEPI.
declarations.funderStatement: Coalition of Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI); Coefficient Giving.

detail.abstract:
Background. Evidence on the expected benefits and costs of many pandemic preparedness measures remains limited. This study estimates expected future losses from pandemics and the expected value of a suite of preparedness investments that enhance vaccine response.

Methods. We forecast pandemic risk using a Poisson-generalized Pareto distribution fit to historical outbreak data. We convert mortality, economic, and learning losses to monetaryterms, and use Monte Carlo simulation to estimate expected losses absent vaccine response. We then introduce a vaccine response model calibrated using an expert survey and precedent from COVID-19 and estimate the net present value (NPV) of status quo vaccine response and the incremental NPV of four preparedness investments: advance manufacturing capacity, prototype vaccine R&D, universal flu vaccine R&D, and improved early warning systems.

Findings. We estimate $4 trillion in expected annual social losses from pandemics. Status quo vaccine response on average offsets 18% of that harm ($17.6 trillion NPV). Amongpreparedness investments, universal influenza vaccine R&D delivers the largest incremental NPV ($2.4 trillion), followed by improved early warning ($436 billion), advance capacity ($269 billion), and prototype vaccine R&D ($256 billion). The combination of the four investments has an NPV of $3.3 trillion.

Interpretation. All four preparedness programs generated benefits exceeding their cost.Universal flu vaccine R&D in particular stands out. The high expected value of status quovaccine response highlights the importance of preserving the capabilities that enabled rapidCOVID-19 vaccine rollout.

title: Partisan Values and Financial Misconduct
affiliations: City University of Hong Kong (CityU) and Villanova University - Department of Finance

detail.title: Partisan Values and Financial Misconduct
detail.abstract: We use self-declared party affiliations from voter registration records as a proxy for individual values and study misconduct among U.S. financial advisers. Comparing advisers who work in the same branch at the same time, Republican-affiliated advisers are 9.6% more likely to have a misconduct disclosure, relative to the mean rate of misconduct. The gap is not explained by experience, qualifications, customer sorting, or alignment with the party in local power. The partisan misconduct gap is concentrated in branches where co partisans predominate, in branches with a history of misconduct, and is close to zero in politically mixed branches. The same in-group dynamics shape the adviser labor market: advisers who are politically aligned with their coworkers are less likely to separate after misconduct, and advisers with a misconduct disclosure re-match to firms whose managers share their political affiliation. Individual values predict professional misconduct where the workplace environment permits their expression.

title: Mapping the Dynamics of Radiation Therapy Workforce Gaps in Cambodia: A Systems-Based Causal Loop Analysis

detail.abstract:
Background: The burden of cancer is increasing in Cambodia but there are substantial unmet radiotherapy (RT) needs. This study aimed to identify and understand the systemic drivers of demand for radiation therapists (RTTs) in Cambodia over the next 10 years.

Methods: A group model-building workshop was conducted by health services researchers involving key stakeholders (n=28) from Cambodia’s RT community. Insights from the workshop supplemented by a literature review, were used to develop a causal loop diagram (CLD). The CLD was subsequently refined and validated through iterative stakeholder feedback and discussion. 

Findings: Demand for radiotherapy services is driven primarily by cancer incidence and the proportion of cases eligible for radiotherapy. Four key feedback loops were identified. First, unmet radiotherapy demand creates a balancing loop whereby treatment delays lead to disease progression, poorer clinical outcomes, and a shift from curative to palliative treatment intent. The second and third feedback loops demonstrate that meeting radiotherapy demand requires sustained investment in both RTT workforce development and radiotherapy equipment capacity. The fourth loop highlights public awareness of the RTT profession as an important driver of enrolment into RTT training programmes and long-term workforce sustainability, as public misconceptions about radiation remain common. 

Interpretation: The CLD identified several key leverage points for reducing unmet radiotherapy needs and improving outcomes for patients with cancers amenable to radiotherapy. These findings can inform workforce and capacity planning to support the sustainable development of radiotherapy services in Cambodia.
